content:
https://github.com/empath-nirvana/polyclone

The short explanation of what it proves is that there is no bivariate polynomial over Z[x,y] whose term-substitution clone (ie: all possible compositions of itself with all integers and X Y), has BOTH X+Y and X*Y

Another way to put it is that there is no single polynomial over the integers that generates all polynomials through composition with itself and integer constants.

There is also a simpler proof for the same result over Zero Sum Free semirings (ie: positive numbers).

There's also a counterexample for polynomials over Q (and any other field that doesn't have a map F2).

I am _not_ a mathematician, but this was the end result of a month long effort to tackle that conjecture and not simply a one-shot claude-written proof. I do understand the problem and the high level description of the proof, and it completely compiles, and really I just wanted a second set of eyes on it to make sure it proves what I think it does.
Please read the rules, you have no Comparator statement using Mathlib only and no formalization.yml.
Is there a document for these rules? I see them referenced here a lot but are they written anywhere?

i added them and add the judge run to CI and it passed:

https://github.com/empath-nirvana/polyclone/actions/runs/27310179480/job/80678155171

I am seeing nothing in the repository that a universal algebraist would read. I see a brief overall description, but no detailed formal proof. I am not seeing any references to the literature, the source of the original problem, or clean universal-algebraic statement. (Is the structure <R,p> where p is complete a primal or idemprimal algebra? Is the statement only about the polynomial clone over R or the full clone over R? Is there any analysis or implication about any Malcev conditions that <R,p> might have? Is there anything beyond the initial readme that does a decent description of the main results and lemmas leading to it, as well as a rationale to why such a formalization might hold?)

I suspect there is no universal algebraist alive who is conversant in Lean enough to read the code directly without a blueprint. I am neither a good researcher in universal algebra nor fluent in Lean, but I have enough expertise to suspect the claim on its own merits, primarily because it has potential for not being stated clearly enough.

If you provide the paper, which should provide not just an informal description of the proof being formalized, but clear statements of the definitions involved and references and ties to the literature, as well as some idea of what work has been done, I might be bothered enough to read the paper. However, I have to understand that you are talking about generating the full polynomial clone on R which is generated by {x+y,x*y}, and not the full clone on R, which may be different for finite R and definitely different for non-finite R, and the description provided in the repository lacks or hides this precision. As far as the code goes, it is likely riddled with misformalizations. I could not make an assertion on the quality of the code without a good blueprint, which I am not finding in the repository.

Having done some work in clone theory in another millennium, I am mildly interested in what the result could be, but the current README and accompanying files that I can understand are woefully insufficient. Also, I don't trust Lean or the experts in Lean enough to say that you have formalized what you hope you have formalized. People are still trying to figure this stuff out, and are still approaching what might be universally accepted as (not misformalized).

Yeah, that's the thing. I'm _not_ mathematician, and _I don't know how to write a math paper_. I'm a software engineer that got to this proof just playing around with a question that I thought would be easy to answer and turned out to be quite complicated. I do have a draft paper written by claude if you want to read that, and a blog post that's a lot more informal. I'm kind of hoping for some help trying to figure out if this is interesting or even worth writing up.

I've attached a draft paper, but I am going HEAVILY CAVEAT THIS. This was written by claude (the new mode, Fable) based on the lean work, I haven't verified any of the references, they might be hallucinated and I don't know enough about the math to know if the paper reflects what is in the proof. I think it's an interesting result, because I was interested in the question and I'm happy with the resolution, but I am not an expert in the field, and do not know if it's novel or interesting. It has my name on the authorship in the draft, but I am not claiming that I wrote this, it's 100% a product of Claude, although the lean code is the result of weeks of work with claude directing it to a solution (it wasn't remotely a one-shot lean proof, where I asked it a question and it gave me the answer--- it took weeks of research and experimentation to get there.)

char2-dichotomy-draft.pdf

For what its worth, i skimmed the PDF, currently I would say it is not really in a readable state. If I were you I would suggest a few changes like , make sure to define every quantity before talking about it, add in-text citations for a lot more things so it can be easier to check.

It's argument at face value could maybe work but I wouldn't take that to mean its true, because it is actually a fairly fragile argument that would completely break down if there was a missed edge case or mistake.

In terms of the lean code, the code itself is pretty juvenile so I am surprised fable would prove things in that way at this late stage. But otherwise it isnt as bad as some AI projects, there are too many files but each one isnt horrifically long at least.

Your comparator doesn't look too bad either, Github action is fine but I had to dig a bit, youd pique more interest signposting it more here:

"it could be something" is where I am with it, but I need help from someone in the field to actually figure out exactly what it is and how to write it up. I don't have remotely an academic background, just a recreational math enthusiast that got stuck on a question and decided to use it as an excuse to try and do a lean proof with claude. I didn't even know what clone theory or universal algebra was 3 weeks ago.

To rely just on lean, you need both a lean expert and the domain knowledge to know for sure. This is often the hard part, and this category of people is very small overall.

A weaker restriction though is someone who knows the domain well and some or little Lean, so the Lean is an extra part. For that, you'd need that PDF cleaned up a lot , or I guess you could pay someone.

Because if it is not formatted in a way an article would be in terms of flow and readability, people's interest probably won't be piqued enough to volunteer their time (if it is a colleague they know or know through a mutual naturally its different, but a complete stranger to math, rougher odds its legit).

So I would start there, and also I guess what is your goal, to convince yourself, or to convince the community broadly and try publish it in a journal? For the former, you can just learn the content yourself if you are interested in the problem ( i assume you picked this problem specifically maybe out of interest ).

John Thompson said:

"it could be something" is where I am with it, but I need help from someone in the field to actually figure out exactly what it is and how to write it up. I don't have remotely an academic background, just a recreational math enthusiast that got stuck on a question and decided to use it as an excuse to try and do a lean proof with claude. I didn't even know what clone theory or universal algebra was 3 weeks ago.

So I am not the professional you would need to prepare/rewrite the manuscript as needed. I do know just enough of the area that I can give you suggestions as to how to rewrite it and whom to ask for professional help.

The choice of the word "complete" in this document is unfortunate; I would recommend that the problem focus on the particular clone (which I will rename temporarily) RPoly which is the abstract set you are considering (polynomial terms in the language of a commutative ring) and its representation as functions over a base set R (the elements of the commutative ring) which you could call R[x,y]. RPoly is the abstract clone generated by the terms (x+y) and (x*y) and projections, and (if you wish) symbols for the constants (0,1, and arbitrary r from the commutative ring), and while Rpoly is large enough for most considerations in algebra, it is not the full clone of terms that can be considered especially if the language is expanded to include additional function symbols (such as minus). So one needs to be clear what terms are considered, and how those terms become represented as functions on R.

Rather than talk about a polynomial or a clone being complete in some sense, you should talk about whether a single polynomial generates the clone Rpoly you are considering. This is the actual problem being tackled, and once this is made clear, a lot of the PDF seems reasonable. There are other technical rephrasings to be suggested, but removing the word "complete" from the paper and replacing it by a more (with respect to the field in which you are trying to find experts) accurate term like "successfully generates" or "fully generates" would go far in making the subject of the paper approachable by the experts you seek.

When I get some more time, I will make a few more suggestions. Meanwhile, be sure to come up with appropriate names for the objects, and try to avoid polynomial clone or similar phrases until you can verify that it matches the technical definition used in books on universal algebra. Making up names for your objects of study and seeing how the named objects relate to the technical definitions is a good exercise for you which I am willing to grade. The paper goes part way in doing this, but you need to be comfortable with this sort of framing before you can ask for professional help.
